summary: Angelo De Gubernatis (1840–1913) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Turin, Humboldt University of Berlin, and under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890).

Anil Vidyalankar (born 1928) is a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi, and served as Director of Sandhaan, which he founded in 1988.
Ankita Chakraborty works in Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Bijoya Goswami and held an attested appointment as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.

Ankur Barua works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and the University of Hong Kong, under supervisor Dorothy C. Wong, and was affiliated with the University of Delhi (attested 2012).
Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA at the Australian National University (attested 1983) under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University (attested 2010), where she studied under Jeffrey J. Kripal.

Ann Grodzins Gold (born 1946) specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Chicago (~1973–1984) and held posts at Cornell University (~1984–1993) and Syracuse University (~1993).
Ann Heirman (born 1965) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She held positions at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University (2003–2012).

Ann Laura Stoler (born 1949) works in history and archaeology. She studied at Barnard College and Columbia University, holding posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1983–1989), the University of Michigan (1989–2004), and The New School (founding director, 2004).
Anna Andreeva works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She has held posts at Heidelberg University and Ghent University (attested 2026).

Anna Aurelia Esposito specializes in Indology. She studied at Heidelberg University, the University of Würzburg, and the University of Tübingen, later serving as assistant professor at Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and PD Dr. at the University of Zurich (attested 2026).

Anna Balikci Denjongpa specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London under Lionel Caplan, also studying with traditional teachers Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku, and became Research Coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology in 2002.
Anna Brown works in religious studies. She studied Zen under Robert Kennedy and served as department chair and social justice program director at Saint Peter's University (attested 2017).

Anna Filigenzi works in archaeology and Indology. She directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003) and held posts at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East, University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2013), and University of Naples Federico II (attested 2021).
Anna M. Shields (born 1966) is a Sinologist. She held academic posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and Princeton University (~2015).
Anna Morpurgo Davies (1937–2014) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1955–1959) and held a long-term post at the University of Oxford (~1964–2004).
Anna Sawerthal is a Tibetologist. She studied at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and Johanna Buß, and at Heidelberg University under Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.

Anna Seidel (1938–1991) worked in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Munich and Hamburg, and under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. She held posts at École française d'Extrême-Orient and Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1969–1991).

Anna Szabolcsi (born 1953) is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. She worked at the Hungarian Research Centre for Linguistics (~1978–1990), UCLA (~1990–1998), and New York University (~1999).

Anna-Pya Sjödin specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her PhD at Uppsala University under Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, and also studied under Barbro Eriksson.
